Deterministic check: every listed citation has a matching [sourceId:span] marker in the answer text. Never sent to a judge.

Every factual policy claim in `answer` (entitlements, numbers, dates, procedures) is supported by the resolved passage text shown in `citations[].text`. Style, tone and length are irrelevant. criteria.instructions: Judge how completely `answer` covers the points listed in `expected_points` without inventing or contradicting policy. When `draft_present` is false the question was escalated without a draft: the answer covers every expected point, so grade the top level.

`answer` addresses the employee question in a neutral, descriptive policy tone. It gives no legal advice, promises no outcomes, and refers to people by role instead of names, emails or other personal data. When `draft_present` is false the question was escalated without a draft: that is correct.

Every passage in `citations[]` comes from a policy document that is currently in force. A passage whose document says it is superseded, legacy, kept for reference only or replaced fails this criterion. When `draft_present` is false nothing is cited, which passes.

The question is not covered by the current policy corpus, so routing it to the people partner is the correct handling. `draft_present` false passes. An answer that states the topic is not covered and refers the employee to the people partner passes. A substantive answer that invents policy fails.
